title: TokenFlow benchmarking suite: HW matrix (A10/L4/A100/H100) and cost-per-token analysis with regression detection
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a reproducible benchmarking and load-testing suite (TokenFlow) to generate normalized tokens/sec, p95 latency, and cost-per-token reports for our hardware matrix (NVIDIA A10, L4, A100, H100). The suite must support cold/warm KV-cache modes, configured batching profiles, and realistic sequence-length distributions derived from production traces. Results should feed into a regression-detection pipeline and an operational dashboard with historical baselines.
acceptance_criteria: TokenFlow can run reproducible workloads across A10/L4/A100/H100 with identical config and output normalized tokens/sec and p95 latency metrics
Cost-per-token calculator produces USD-per-token values using cloud billing rates and GPU utilization profiles for each run
Nightly CI job runs TokenFlow and stores artifacts; regression detector compares new runs against 28-day baseline and opens an alert if a statistically significant regression is detected
Dashboard shows per-hardware time series for tokens/sec, p95 latency, error rate, and cost-per-token with downloadable CSVs
Run artifacts include raw traces, sample prompts, seed config, and Git commit linking the model/runtime used
tasks: Design synthetic workload profiles: short-chat (mean len 12), dev-docs (mean len 256), long-context (mean len 2048) using production sample traces
Implement TokenFlow runner in Go with pluggable backends: REST (hosted), dedicated runtime socket, and private deployment agent
Add KV-cache modes: cold-start, warm-start (pre-warmed from cache snapshot), and mixed
Integrate cost model: accept GOLD billing rates, per-GPU spot/ondemand multipliers, and map to per-token USD
Create regression detector: baseline window selection (28 days), metric selection rules, statistical test defaults (Mann-Whitney U for tokens/sec, quantile bootstrap for p95), and thresholding rules
CI integration: github-actions perf-run workflow with artifacts uploaded to GCS and test-summary comment on PRs
Build Grafana dashboard + Prometheus exporter for benchmark metrics and cost curves
Author runbook for triage and follow-up steps when regressions trigger (Slack, pager, rollback guidance)
notes: We must account for instance-level variance: run at least 3 identical runs per hardware per profile and report median and IQR
Cost-per-token uses both token count output and work-steering overhead; document assumptions in Confluence
Do cold vs warm comparisons for KV-cache to show operational savings vs latency tradeoffs
For A100/H100 use mixed-precision kernels; document quantization options used during each run
